messages:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH - us-east-1 gpu-hotpath pool reporting sustained 429s (-> 60% above threshold) and queue growth. Affected customers: several mid-tier Dedicated tenants. Auto-escalate to #incidents. Priority: P1.

mia: seeing the same in metrics — queue depth on hotpath up from 120 -> 950 over last 6m. latency p95 jumping to 2.1s after initial auth windows.

sam: adding context: autoscaler attempted scale but got stuck in WAIT state; max_replicas for this pool is 12 and current pods = 12. Rate-limiter logs show tokenbucket refill failure for tier=mid-heavy.

raj: @mia can you paste the autoscaler logs? i want the timeline.

mia: sure, tail from last 20m:

```
2026-03-15T18:22:03Z autoscaler: step(scale) target=us-east-1/gpu-hotpath desired=16 -> bounded by max=12
2026-03-15T18:23:47Z tokenbucket: tier=mid-heavy refill_rate=0.8r/s configured_units=units_per_min=48
2026-03-15T18:24:02Z proxy: 429 -> downstream=tokenbucket: insufficient_tokens
2026-03-15T18:25:10Z autoscaler: cooldown active, last_scale=30s, skip
2026-03-15T18:27:51Z queue: pending_requests=912
```

kim: interesting — config says refill_rate=0.8r/s for that tier; expected is 8r/s. looks like a decimal place got lost in a recent rollout of ratepolicy-service.

oncall-ops: paging infra owner @sam for immediate mitigation.

sam: on it. first mitigation: promote a temporary higher-tier token bucket for hotpath to bypass the misconfigured tier. applying patch now.

support-bot: noticed customer #acme-analytics reporting errors: "Model request failed: 429" since 18:24. They have Dedicated capacity; impact is degraded throughput.

raj: while sam works on tokenbucket, we should also enable fallback routing to the backup pool (gpu-warmpath-small) for mid-tier requests to stop queue growth. can someone toggle routing?

sam: applying routing override:
```
POST /admin/routing/override
{
  "match_tier": "mid-heavy",
  "route_to": "gpu-warmpath-small",
  "duration_sec": 900
}
```
patched. routing override active.

mia: after override, pending_requests dropped from 912 -> 340 over 90s. 429 rate decreased but not gone.

kim: tokenbucket patch deployed: we rolled forward a hotfix to ratepolicy-service to restore refill_rate to 8r/s for mid-heavy. pushing now.

sam: confirm tokenbucket values in runtime:
```
> curl -s http://rates.us-east-1/internal/tier/mid-heavy | jq '.refill_rate'
8.0
```

mia: nice — seeing immediate improvement. 429s back to baseline in last 60s. queue now 120.

support-bot: notified impacted customers with ETA: hotfix applied, routing override in place, monitoring for 30m.

raj: root cause hypothesis: deployment of ratepolicy-service 2.14.0 introduced a parsing bug that dropped a trailing zero on refill rates when loading YAML defaults for legacy tier names. it affected only the mid-heavy legacy mapping.

kim: yes, confirmed in the release diff: change to parseFloat usage. unit tests missed legacy alias case.

sam: mitigation plan: 1) revert to 2.13.7 for ratepolicy-service in us-east-1 as short-term. 2) patch parser + add regression tests. 3) audit tier mappings for other regions. 4) consider safety limits so buckets can't be < 1r/s for production tiers.

mia: rolling rollback now for us-east-1 ratepolicy-service to 2.13.7 (canary -> full).

incident-bot: Deploy job started: deploy/ratepolicy-service us-east-1 -> 2.13.7 (canary)

sam: can we also temporarily bump the pool max_replicas to 20 while we validate rollback? that'll give autoscaler headroom until we confirm token refills.

kim: increased max_replicas to 20 on gpu-hotpath. autoscaler accepted new limit.

mia: graph update: after max bump and routing override the queue stabilized under 80. 429s < 0.5% of requests now.

support-bot: customer comms sent to affected tenants: explanation + steps we took + timeline. one customer asked for SLA credit estimation; notify CS.

raj: postmortem notes to capture: misparse bug in ratepolicy-service, insufficient regression coverage for legacy alias, no safety floor for refill_rate, autoscaler limit prevented immediate scale. Also route override and temporary max_replicas change were effective mitigations.

oncall-ops: handing off to follow-up rotation: @kim and @raj will lead postmortem and remediation tomorrow morning. @mia will keep monitoring for next 2 hours.

sam: follow ups I own: revert confirmed -> done, add guardrails to config loader, create alert for refill_rate < 1r/s.

kim: I'll open PR for parser fix and add unit+integration tests that cover legacy aliases.

mia: closing live incident channel after monitoring period. will post final timeline summary here. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident update: status = mitigated. monitoring = 30m. severity = P1 -> investigating -> mitigated.

mia: final notes (to include in postmortem): timeline, affected customer list, exact config diff, commands used for routing override, and follow-ups with owners. will drop draft in #postmortems within 24h.

support-bot: logged customer tickets and relayed SLA credit requests to billing.

raj: thanks all — nice quick coordination. lessons: add improvable checks on deploys that change numeric defaults. :thumbsup:

mia: thread archived for now."
